summary: Added the shared bounded log-subject policy/helper at src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs (ADR-026 clauses 1-2). LogSubject.Create(Guid jellyfinItemId, string? primaryPath) returns the file-name component only via Path.GetFileName (never a directory, drive, share, or parent path) and LogSubject.Create(Guid jellyfinItemId) is the item-id-only overload; both fall back to the Jellyfin item identifier in D format whenever no usable name is available. The file name is bounded to the documented LogSubject.MaximumScalarValues = 128 Unicode scalar values, has control scalars removed, and is otherwise emitted verbatim (whitespace is not collapsed or trimmed), all in one scalar-wise pass so a surrogate pair is never split; an empty, whitespace, control-only, or control-reduced-to-whitespace name falls back to the item id, and the helper never throws for a null, empty, whitespace, or unusable path. tests/ArrTags.Tests/LogSubjectTests.cs adds 23 cases covering file-name-only, the bound (at-bound/over-bound/surrogate-pair safety), control removal, empty/whitespace fallback, non-ASCII/combining verbatim handling, and the D-format item-id fallback. Task 15.1 is the helper and policy only: threading through the call sites is 15.2, the render classification is 15.3, and the ADR-020 amendment/canonical docs/security review are 15.4; limitation F8 remains open.

interpretations.question: Does the 128-scalar bound apply before or after control-character removal?
interpretations.chosen: Control scalars are skipped first and do not count toward the bound; the bound is applied to the control-free text.
interpretations.basis: ADR-026 clause 2 does not fix the order; the clause 'reduces to nothing after normalization' implies normalization includes control removal, and bounding the normalized text preserves the most usable content while still yielding at most 128 control-free scalars.
interpretations.impact: A name with many leading controls followed by text keeps the text instead of truncating to an empty fallback. The emitted subject remains within the ADR bounds; no persisted or user-visible state is affected. Covered by BoundIsAppliedAfterControlRemoval.

interpretations.question: How is whitespace treated inside and around the file name?
interpretations.chosen: Whitespace is emitted verbatim (not collapsed or trimmed); only a name that is entirely whitespace, or that reduces to entirely whitespace after control removal, falls back to the item id.
interpretations.basis: ADR-026 clause 2 says the file name is 'otherwise emitted verbatim' and only an empty/whitespace/reduced-to-nothing name falls back. ADR-026 does not ask for the BadgeTextNormalizer whitespace-collapsing behavior.
interpretations.impact: Log subjects can contain the file name's exact spacing. No persisted or user-visible state; covered by ControlRemovalDoesNotCollapseOrTrimWhitespace and NamesThatReduceToNothingOrWhitespaceFallBackToTheItemIdentifier.

interpretations.question: How are Windows-style paths treated when the helper runs on a non-Windows host?
interpretations.chosen: Path.GetFileName's host-platform separator semantics are used unchanged.
interpretations.basis: ADR-026 clause 1 explicitly names Path.GetFileName; Jellyfin reports host-native paths, so on the pinned Linux host a backslash is a valid character of a Linux file name rather than a separator.
interpretations.impact: On the pinned Linux host a literal 'C:\dir\file.mkv' string would be emitted as a file name containing backslashes (such a string is not a Linux path); drive/parent components are never emitted on Windows hosts. No directory derived from a host-native path can be emitted.

interpretations.question: Should Guid.Empty be rejected?
interpretations.chosen: Accepted and formatted; the helper never throws.
interpretations.basis: The task and ADR-026 require the helper to be fallback-safe and never throw into a caller; the item id is a non-null value type and the all-zeros identifier leaks nothing.
interpretations.impact: A caller passing Guid.Empty emits the all-zeros D string rather than failing a log call.
